extracted.intended_audience: public relations students and practitioners (communications professionals learning press-release craft)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing effective press releases within public relations, covering pre-writing decisions, format and style standards, news framing, persuasion principles, and special release types. Oriented toward producing newsworthy, audience-targeted releases that follow professional/AP style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: State clearly what action you want the release to produce (the specific purpose of the release).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-writing consideration: identify the desired outcome up front — media pick-up, public action, attendance, fundraising, etc. Keep purpose central to content and call-to-action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the multiple audiences the release should reach; tailor message accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that audiences may be plural (media, consumers, stakeholders); use language, tone, and angles appropriate to each; prioritize primary audience in lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate channel/format
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the channel and format that best deliver the message to the intended audience (e.g., wire, email, newsroom posting, social).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel/format choice affects length, packaging (media kit attachments), and timing; match format conventions (e.g., short PSA vs. full news release).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider timing and competition for attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan release timing with awareness of competing news and audience availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing affects pickup — avoid major competing events, use embargoes when appropriate, and consider news cycles and reporters' deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine 'news peg'
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the specific angle or timeliness that makes the content newsworthy (the 'news peg').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong news peg ties the organization’s information to broader public interest or timeliness; use it to justify front-loading the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard letterhead with logo
rubrics_metrics.description: Use official letterhead with organization logo on the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps establish credibility and source identification; place identity where journalists can quickly see origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release timing notation ('For Immediate Release' or embargo)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the release is for immediate distribution or under embargo with clear notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put 'For Immediate Release' or specific embargo date/time prominently; embargoes must be explicit and reliable to respect journalist trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information at top
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide name, title, phone, and email of media contact at the top of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reporters can quickly reach a spokesperson; include multiple contacts if useful for different audiences or regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline above
rubrics_metrics.description: Place a succinct, newsworthy headline above the lead to summarize the key point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline should be clear, active, and entice the reader; avoid jargon; reflect the release’s main news peg.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline at start of first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the first paragraph with the dateline (city — date) to situate the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dateline gives geographic and temporal context; place it at the start of the lead per standard news format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body in inverted pyramid
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the body so most important information comes first, followed by supporting details and background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the inverted-pyramid/News Triangle approach: lead (most newsworthy), middle (supporting details), bottom (background/less critical). This facilitates editorial trimming.

rubrics_metrics.name: End mark ('###' or '-30-')
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclude the release with a conventional end mark such as '###' or '-30-'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals to editors that copy ends here; helps avoid truncation or accidental inclusion of notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP Style throughout
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to Associated Press (AP) style conventions consistently in punctuation, capitalization, numbers, titles, and other style matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AP for journalist-friendly copy; consistent styling increases pickup and professional appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Write primarily in active voice instead of passive constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active voice produces clearer, more direct copy and stronger leads; prefer subject-verb-object constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short sentences (15-20 words avg)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep sentence length concise, targeting an average of about 15–20 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short sentences improve readability and make it easier for journalists to scan and edit; avoid long, convoluted sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short paragraphs (1-3 sentences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use brief paragraphs, typically one to three sentences each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short paragraphs increase readability and fit newsroom layout conventions; each paragraph should present a single idea or fact cluster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete words over abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor concrete, specific wording instead of abstract or vague language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete details (names, numbers, specifics) make the release more newsworthy and verifiable; avoid generic platitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific over general
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific facts and examples rather than generalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specificity supports credibility and usefulness for reporters — include quantifiable facts, dates, names, and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid jargon and acronyms
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimize or explain technical jargon and acronyms that may confuse general audiences or reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When acronyms are necessary, spell them out on first reference per AP style; favor plain-language equivalents where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use second references (avoid repetition)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the first full reference, use concise second references (e.g., last names, shortened organization names) to avoid repetition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow journalistic practice: full identification on first mention, then shorter references to maintain flow and avoid redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five W's + H in the lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer Who, What, When, Where, Why, and How in the lead paragraph, front-loading the most important facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lead should summarize the essential facts immediately; reporters and editors expect key facts up front for quick decisions and trimming.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Triangle (lead, supporting, background)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure content according to the News Triangle: top (lead with most newsworthy info), middle (supporting details), bottom (background/less critical information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This model guides how to order material to serve editors' need for quick cuts and readers' need for clarity; it complements the inverted-pyramid approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasion — source credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish credible sources to support claims in the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authoritative quotes, named spokespersons, data sources, and third-party validation to enhance persuasion and trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasion — message clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft a clear, focused persuasive message that is easy to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mixed messages; ensure the core claim and call-to-action are explicit and repeated succinctly where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasion — audience-appropriate appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor appeals (emotional, rational, ethical) to the values and interests of the identified audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose evidence, tone, and calls-to-action that resonate with the target audiences rather than generic messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasion — evidence and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Support persuasive claims with concrete evidence and illustrative examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statistics, case examples, quotes, or anecdotes that substantiate claims and make them reportable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasion — ethical persuasion (no manipulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persuade without manipulating; maintain ethical standards in messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid deceptive or coercive tactics; be transparent about motivations and avoid misleading framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special press release types covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of different release-related formats: standard news release, media kit elements, public service announcement, brochure copy, newsletter article, annual report content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different types have different length, tone, and packaging requirements — choose the appropriate type and adapt style/format accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serves specific identified purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should clearly serve the specific purpose identified in pre-writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate releases by whether content and call-to-action align with the stated purpose (media outreach, event promotion, awareness, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Targets identified audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should be targeted to the audiences identified during planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether language, examples, channel, and news peg fit the intended audiences and their interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follows AP style and standard format
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should conform to AP style and the standard press-release format described (letterhead, contact, dateline, lead, inverted pyramid, end mark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conformity increases the likelihood of pickup and ease of use by journalists; nonconforming releases are more likely to be edited out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-loads news in 5Ws
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should put the most important facts (the 5Ws+H) in the lead paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-loading facilitates editorial decision-making and supports readers' quick comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses active voice
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should consistently use active constructions for clarity and strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active voice enhances readability and makes attribution and action clearer for journalists and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses concrete language
rubrics_metrics.description: The release should use concrete, specific language rather than abstractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete language improves credibility and makes material easier to report directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has credible source/quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a credible quote or named source to add authority and human interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-chosen quotes humanize the story and provide usable sound bites for media; ensure spokespeople are prepared and credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has clear next steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear call-to-action or next steps for the audience (what readers should do next).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Next steps might include registration links, contact instructions, donation directions, or media-arrival details; make them prominent and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edited rigorously
rubrics_metrics.description: The release must be carefully edited for accuracy, clarity, grammar, and style before distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigorously edit to remove errors, tighten language, verify facts, and ensure adherence to AP style and organizational messaging.
